paragraphs: Chapter 808
Episode 201. The Invasion Begins (1)

Before the start of the Ill-Omen War, Zipple had closed all Magic Towers except for the first-class ones. They supplied fleets and troops to each area of the federation and built new Magic Towers according to the water supply level.
The second-class Magic Tower that the enemy tribe invaded this time was mid-tier. It was fortified with about fifty fleets and around a thousand magicians.

The flagship was an Arcadia-class from Zipple's headquarters and the tower master was a non-Zipple-born 8-star magician. However, two phantom troops and ghost squads were also deployed, each with combat power surpassing the tower master. Although not the very elite, it was not lacking to be called an elite.
And it only took 30 minutes for the enemy tribe to obliterate the second-class Magic Tower.
Even though it was an entirely unexpected attack, the Magic Tower in Ramatan could not even fight back properly and ended up in ashes.
"...Are you saying there was such a big difference in the fleet's power?"

Veradin asked. A complete ruin was spread out on the land where the grand second-class Magic Tower once stood. The black bone fragments left in various parts of the ruin suggested that the enemy tribe's bombardment was extremely brutal.
The only survivors of the raid were two people from Satrien's ghost squad.

"Yes, lord. Suddenly, a huge dimensional gate opened in the sky and more than a hundred enemy tribe ships appeared. They were far superior to our fleet. Even though most of our fleets couldn't launch properly, even if they had fought prepared, the only difference would have been in the battle time. The outcome would not have been different."
The surviving ghost squad explained the situation to Veradin and bowed their heads.
"Did they seem to be superior to the fleet Jin faced?"
"...Yes. Although the enemy tribe hardly disembarked, so I couldn't confirm, but it seemed like their commander was not Rakiman Hog, but someone else."
"What made you think that?"
"The emblem on the fleet was different."
"Is that all? Are you saying they didn't declare war or even tell us their purpose?"

"They didn't say a single word. As soon as the dimensional gate opened, they started bombing. The top of the tower fell apart from the first bombardment, causing the tower master to die. Although I took over the command and started responding immediately... there was nothing I could do."
Indeed, the enemy tribe silently carried out a one-sided massacre and then disappeared in an instant. Just like Diphus and Joshua, who were thrown into chaos just before the Ill-Omen War.
It was an attack that could only be carried out if large-scale teleportation was possible.
However, unlike then, the enemy tribe did not cause any harm to civilians. They strictly destroyed only the Magic Towers and left.

"I originally wanted to have a conversation with them once, but since they attacked us first, there seems to be no choice but to fight. I get the feeling they've already joined hands with others. We're deeply embroiled with those lunatics. Why on earth did they attack us? They wouldn't have done this just to show off their power."
"After the Magic Tower was destroyed, ropes came down from the ship. We saw them capturing the strong magicians who survived the bombardment. We almost got caught too."

"I don't think their goal was to use them as prisoners. If that were the case, they would have targeted the tower master or other key figures first, and they would have told us what they wanted before they left."
Veradin recalled what he recently heard from Sanna.

"In addition, I heard from a shaman that among the ancient tribes in the underground, there are those that feed on the blood of other lives. I think they're the enemy tribe. They also said that there were hardly any bodies left in the destroyed Kinzelo Beastmen's local branch. They must have caught everyone to take their blood."
Hoo...
Veradin sighed and shook his head.
"We are ashamed."
The ghost squads bowed their heads.
"It's not your fault. Rather, you deserve credit for surviving and informing us about the size and combat power of the attackers. If you have any requests, speak to the judge."
Veradin waved the ghost squads away and exchanged glances with the officers.
"I never imagined that we'd be attacked like this by those who are not even from Runcandel or Kinzelo. It's shameful that such an incident happened when you haven't been lord for long."

"The family's prestige is not important, Jin ruined it a long time ago. The problem isn't our reputation or the immediate damage, but the fact that we couldn't respond at all to their attack, Phantom Captain. Since they harvested without any damage, they will continue to attack various parts of the federation like this."
"For the time being, all areas must maintain a state of emergency. However, I'm worried because the fleet gap is said to be so extreme."

"All we need to do is hold out until we recognize the attack and send reinforcements. They held out for 30 minutes when they were attacked in an unguarded state, so if they're fully prepared, they should be able to hold out for at least two hours."

"I don't think the enemy tribe's spatial movement is without any restrictions, Lord. I don't think they can conduct an attack by operating a fleet of over a hundred ships every time. If they attack our area on a smaller scale, we can buy more time."
"I think so too, Brother Ronil. We need to deploy the small high-speed ships that are being tested to all areas first. So they can immediately report to the top if any place is attacked."

"All ground-based transit gates are still closed due to the residual aura left by Gleac. Excluding a very few capable of space leaps or long-distance communication, the fastest means of transportation in the present world was Zipple's high-speed ships.

"The war with the Red Plutonian has begun as of now. We will have to fight a disadvantageous battle for the time being due to a lack of information. The most urgent thing is to find out where they're based."
"I will order to capture at least one Red Plutonian alive in every battle. Even if it requires some sacrifices."

"Do so, brother. It will be more beneficial to capture one Red Plutonian alive even if we lose another magic tower. And don't cover up what happened today. It was such a terrible defeat that we can't hide it awkwardly."
It would have been possible to cover up such humiliation with historical manipulation if the Magic Stone was in a better state than now, but it wasn't.
"What should I do?"
"Jin. Publish an article that casts doubt on the collusion between the Vamel Alliance and the Red Plutonian."
"Understood."

"It's an obvious incitement, but the important thing is to make the public aware that the new threat of the Red Plutonian arriving on the surface originated from Jin. Hurry. It's better to have the article out before the Red Plutonian attack Runcandel or the Vamel Alliance."
"Yes, Your Honor. In fact, the Red Plutonian deliberately avoided civilian casualties this time, which is consistent with the Vamel Alliance's methods. I'll focus the article on that."

"But it's strange, Your Honor. According to the report of the Phantom Troops, the Red Plutonian seems to have some form of grudge against Jin, but I don't understand why they attacked us first with their forces. They could have inflicted quite a lot of damage if they attacked Hupester and the forts and castles of the empire, even if attacking the Garden of the Sword or Tikan was too much."
At Octavia's words, Ronil nodded. Veradin's eyes narrowed.
"Fear."
"Your Honor?"

"I have an intuition, somehow, that they're afraid of Jin. Just a while ago, in Kinzelo 3, a whole fleet and a high-ranking Red Plutonian were almost completely destroyed by one Jin. Both attacking us first and avoiding civilian casualties may be because they don't want to provoke Jin for the time being."
Veradin turned around and started walking towards Cozek.
"So let's show them who's the scarier adversary."

"Veradin will definitely release an article saying we woke up the Red Plutonian. Something like, as if it wasn't enough that Runcandel gave birth to a monstrosity, they are once again collaborating with underground forces and threatening the world. Looking at how Veradin has been manipulating public opinion recently, it's a certainty."
Jin accurately predicted Veradin's move.

"You're an expert at undermining authority, but Zipple has been unusually active in the media lately. Wasn't it decided not to care about that anymore? I feel like there might be another reason, not just to justify war."

"You're right, Quicantel. A thought just occurred to me, perhaps the media war, shifting the threat of the world onto me, might be groundwork for eventual historical manipulation. The more people believe it, the easier it will be to manipulate."
"Wow... that's chilling, Jin. That's possible. But we have Valeria, so we should be okay!"

"It's just a guess, Enya. Anyway, the more pressing issue right now is the movements of Zipple and the Red Plutonian. This time they targeted Zipple, but next time it could be us or the Empire. We have communication devices and the Red Owl, so we can respond much faster than Zipple, but we lack a fleet. We can't send fleets ready for battle to all areas like Zipple does."
The underground construction yard of Geomhwangji is still not complete.

"We haven't completed the mass production of Ello yet. The Magic Knights aren't ready to be deployed in all areas. So first, we need to increase the production speed of the communication devices and distribute them to all major bases and forts. In case of a Red Plutonian attack, Nana and other superhumans should be able to respond to the call at any time."
In a word, what Runcandel and the Vamel Alliance needed most was time.

[Jin, their speed is not ordinary. The remnants of the royal family, or whoever they traded with, they must know the Red Plutonian well. They are supplying exactly what the Red Plutonian need to regain their strength. The blood of the outstanding ones, and the information of the world.]
"Ameris, didn't you say last time that the Red Plutonian have the technology to make their fallen soldiers fight again?"
[I did. The Red Plutonian make a biological weapon called the Immortal Army using the hearts of their fallen warriors. Why do you ask that all of a sudden?]
A sinister thought was pricking at Jin's mind.
'If it's true that the remnants of the royal family made a trade... the best thing they could get from the Red Plutonian would be the technology to weaponize Temar's physical body.'
Jin didn't voice his thought and just shook his head.
"It's nothing. Just a passing thought. For now, I'll return to my clan to review troop deployment and come back. Please contact me if there's something that needs to be informed immediately."
"Understood, Scholar."
As Jin was heading to the Garden of the Sword on the Red Owl,
The Red Plutonian were opening another dimensional gate above the world's sky for invasion. It was the sky above the Empire, the sky that Dante was guarding.
